title: Flattening Nested Data
goal: Collapse nested collections into a single continuous iterator stream.

sections.text: When an operation produces a collection for each item, `.map()` creates nested iterators. You will recognise this shape from nested loops in other languages.

sections.caption: flat_map combines mapping and flattening into one adapter.

sections.text: Using `.map()` here produces an iterator of iterators. Downstream adapters would receive inner `Chars` iterators instead of individual `char` items, triggering type mismatch error `E0308`.
`.flat_map()` calls the closure on each element and flattens the resulting inner iterators into a single continuous stream. You will recognise `flat_map` from `flatMap` in JavaScript or Java.

sections.caption: flatten works when items are already iterable.

sections.text: If items are already collections, use `.flatten()` directly. Iterators are lazy, so flattening does not allocate intermediate vectors for each inner stream.

explanation: Collapse nested collections into a single continuous iterator stream.
